name: multi_factor_regression
description: Per-group multiple regression of `response` on `regressors` (auto-intercept): alpha, a beta per regressor, and R² over a distributed OlsFit Gram-matrix aggregate.
source:
# Example operator template (ADR-0020) — a config-driven version of the
# built-in `factor_regression`, showing the three constructs that make
# templates expressive: an input SPLAT, a FAN-OUT (`for_each`), and a
# loop-positional value (`{{ordinal}}`).
#
# Run it:
#   quant-fabric local --templates ./templates \
#     --template multi_factor_regression \
#     --arg data=returns.parquet --arg group_by=date \
#     --arg response=stock_ret --arg regressors=mkt,smb,hml
#
# Emits, per `group_by` group: alpha (intercept), one beta per regressor, and R².
# The `ols_fit` aggregate lowers to DuckDB finalizer UDFs:
# ols_fit_coef(...), ols_fit_r2(...), ols_fit_residual_variance(...),
# ols_fit_stderr(...), and ols_fit_n(...).

[[template]]
name = "multi_factor_regression"
description = "Per-group multiple regression of `response` on `regressors` (auto-intercept): alpha, a beta per regressor, and R² over a distributed OlsFit Gram-matrix aggregate."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"          # the single `table` input becomes the query's data source
kind = "table"
[[template.inputs]]
name = "group_by"
kind = "column"
[[template.inputs]]
name = "response"
kind = "column"
[[template.inputs]]
name = "regressors"
kind = "columns"       # a list — comma-separated on the CLI

[template.plan]
group_by = ["{{group_by}}"]
source_sql = "SELECT * FROM input"
abi_version = 2

# A named input vector: `{{response}}` resolves to one column, `{{regressors}}`
# splats to all of them, in order. OlsFit reads inputs[0] as the response and
# inputs[1..] as the regressors (an intercept is added at design index 0).
[template.plan.vectors]
design = ["{{response}}", "{{regressors}}"]

# Static aggregates.
[[template.plan.aggregate]]
output = "alpha"
function = "ols_fit"
inputs = "@design"
params = { statistic = 0, index = 0 }   # statistic 0 = coefficient; index 0 = intercept

[[template.plan.aggregate]]
output = "r2"
function = "ols_fit"
inputs = "@design"
params = { statistic = 1, index = 0 }   # statistic 1 = R²

# Fan-out: one aggregate per regressor. `{{item}}` is the current column name;
# `{{ordinal}}` is its 1-based position — exactly the OLS design index of
# regressor i (the intercept sits at 0).
[[template.plan.aggregate]]
for_each = "regressors"
output = "beta_{{item}}"
function = "ols_fit"
inputs = "@design"
params = { statistic = 0, index = "{{ordinal}}" }

name: altman_z_score
description: Altman Z-Score bankruptcy-risk discriminant from five firm-level accounting ratios, emitted as a new `output` column.
source:
# altman_z_score
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Altman Z-Score — the classic bankruptcy-prediction discriminant for public
# manufacturers. Combines five balance-sheet / income ratios into one score:
#
#     Z = 1.2 * (working_capital / total_assets)
#       + 1.4 * (retained_earnings / total_assets)
#       + 3.3 * (EBIT / total_assets)
#       + 0.6 * (market_value_equity / total_liabilities)
#       + 1.0 * (sales / total_assets)
#
# Interpretation (original 1968 model): Z > 2.99 = "safe" zone, 1.81 < Z < 2.99 =
# "grey" zone, Z < 1.81 = "distress" zone.
#
# UDF: altman_z(working_capital, retained_earnings, ebit, market_value_equity,
#               sales, total_assets, total_liabilities)  -> z_score
# (septenary scalar; returns NULL when total_assets <= 0 or total_liabilities <= 0)
#
# All seven inputs are firm-level accounting scalars (config), so each is bound
# to a NUMBER input with a realistic literal — none are per-row market columns.
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *,
#          altman_z(20.0, 40.0, 10.0, 200.0, 150.0, 100.0, 100.0) AS z_score
#   FROM input;
#   -- Z = 1.2*0.2 + 1.4*0.4 + 3.3*0.1 + 0.6*2.0 + 1.0*1.5 = 4.01 (safe zone)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[template]]
name = "altman_z_score"
description = "Altman Z-Score bankruptcy-risk discriminant from five firm-level accounting ratios, emitted as a new `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "working_capital"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "retained_earnings"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "ebit"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "market_value_equity"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "sales"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "total_assets"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "total_liabilities"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, altman_z({{working_capital}}, {{retained_earnings}}, {{ebit}}, {{market_value_equity}}, {{sales}}, {{total_assets}}, {{total_liabilities}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { working_capital = 20.0, retained_earnings = 40.0, ebit = 10.0, market_value_equity = 200.0, sales = 150.0, total_assets = 100.0, total_liabilities = 100.0, output = "z_score" }

source:
# =============================================================================
# Template: black76_price
# Category: Derivatives
#
# Prices a European option on a futures / forward using the Black-76 model.
# This is the forward variant of Black-Scholes: the underlying is the forward
# (or futures) price rather than spot, and there is no separate carry/dividend
# term — only a discount factor on the rate.
#
# UDF signature (verified against source):
#   black76_price(opt_type: varchar, forward, strike, ttm, rate, vol) -> double
#     opt_type  - 'call' or 'put'            (column -> opt_type)
#     forward   - forward / futures price    (column -> spot)
#     strike    - option strike              (number)
#     ttm       - time to maturity, years    (number)
#     rate      - risk-free rate (discount)  (number)
#     vol       - volatility                 (column -> vol)
#
# Per-row market inputs (opt_type, forward, vol) are bound to dataset columns;
# scalar contract config (strike, ttm, rate) are Number inputs.
#
# Run it:
#   black76_price(opt_type='call', forward=100, strike=100, ttm=0.5,
#                 rate=0.02, vol=0.2)  ->  ~5.55
# =============================================================================

[[template]]

name: option_greeks
description: COMPOSITE projection (per-row, not aggregate): Black-Scholes Greeks (delta, gamma, vega, theta, rho) as five new columns from one option/market row.
source:
# option_greeks — Black-Scholes option Greeks
#
# CLASSIFICATION: COMPOSITE / projection template — NOT an aggregate.
#   Runs per row (one option/market row in → the same row plus Greek columns
#   out), embarrassingly parallel, with no distributed merge/finalize. It is
#   not a group rollup or global reduce.
#
# Emits the five first/second-order Black-Scholes Greeks in a single SELECT:
#   delta, gamma, vega, theta, rho
# Each Greek is computed by its own UDF from the SAME argument set, so the
# template is a COMPOSITE (multiple output columns, no single `output` input).
#
# PERF NOTE: this calls five separate UDFs over identical args, so shared
# intermediates (d1, d2, N(d1)/n(d1), discount factors, sqrt(ttm)) are recomputed
# five times. For hot paths the better long-term primitive is a single
# `bs_greeks(...) -> STRUCT`/table UDF that computes them once — tracked as a
# follow-up in cgpt-queue/285. This template stays correct and clear meanwhile.
#
# SAFETY/QUOTING: `opt_type` is a COLUMN of 'call'/'put' values, interpolated as a
# quoted identifier (it reads that column). There is no string-literal input kind,
# so a bound value can never inject SQL — but you also cannot pass a bare literal
# like `call`; price a fixed type by giving your data an `opt_type` column.
#
# UDF signature (verified against quant-core / duckdb-quant source):
#   bs_delta(opt_type:varchar, spot, strike, ttm, rate, vol, div)
#   bs_gamma(opt_type:varchar, spot, strike, ttm, rate, vol, div)
#   bs_vega (opt_type:varchar, spot, strike, ttm, rate, vol, div)
#   bs_theta(opt_type:varchar, spot, strike, ttm, rate, vol, div)
#   bs_rho  (opt_type:varchar, spot, strike, ttm, rate, vol, div)
#
# Per-row market inputs are columns: opt_type, spot, strike, vol.
# Scalar config is supplied as numeric literals: ttm, rate, div.
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *,
#     bs_delta('call', 100, 100, 0.5, 0.02, 0.2, 0.0) AS delta,
#     bs_gamma('call', 100, 100, 0.5, 0.02, 0.2, 0.0) AS gamma,
#     bs_vega ('call', 100, 100, 0.5, 0.02, 0.2, 0.0) AS vega,
#     bs_theta('call', 100, 100, 0.5, 0.02, 0.2, 0.0) AS theta,
#     bs_rho  ('call', 100, 100, 0.5, 0.02, 0.2, 0.0) AS rho
#   FROM input;

[[template]]
name = "option_greeks"
description = "COMPOSITE projection (per-row, not aggregate): Black-Scholes Greeks (delta, gamma, vega, theta, rho) as five new columns from one option/market row."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "opt_type"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "spot"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "strike"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "vol"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "ttm"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "rate"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "div"
kind = "number"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, bs_delta({{opt_type}}, {{spot}}, {{strike}}, {{ttm}}, {{rate}}, {{vol}}, {{div}}) AS delta, bs_gamma({{opt_type}}, {{spot}}, {{strike}}, {{ttm}}, {{rate}}, {{vol}}, {{div}}) AS gamma, bs_vega({{opt_type}}, {{spot}}, {{strike}}, {{ttm}}, {{rate}}, {{vol}}, {{div}}) AS vega, bs_theta({{opt_type}}, {{spot}}, {{strike}}, {{ttm}}, {{rate}}, {{vol}}, {{div}}) AS theta, bs_rho({{opt_type}}, {{spot}}, {{strike}}, {{ttm}}, {{rate}}, {{vol}}, {{div}}) AS rho FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { opt_type = "opt_type", spot = "spot", strike = "strike", vol = "vol", ttm = 0.5, rate = 0.02, div = 0.0 }

name: exposure_summary
description: COMPOSITE projection (per-row, not aggregate): exposure breakdown (gross/net/long/short) over a signed position column plus a leverage ratio against a Number NAV.
source:
# =============================================================================
# Template: exposure_summary
# Category: Exposures
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# COMPOSITE template that derives a per-row portfolio exposure breakdown from a
# single signed position/market-value column, plus a portfolio leverage ratio.
#
# Emits five new columns in one SELECT:
#   gross  = gross_exposure(pos)   -> |position|            (unary)
#   net    = net_exposure(pos)     -> position (signed)     (unary)
#   long   = long_exposure(pos)    -> max(position, 0)      (unary)
#   short  = short_exposure(pos)   -> min(position, 0)|abs  (unary)
#   leverage = leverage(gross_exposure(pos), nav)           (binary)
#
# `nav` (net asset value) is a scalar Number config input, not a column.
# As a COMPOSITE there is no single `output` input.
#
# Run it:
#   from quant_fabric import run_template
#   run_template(
#       "exposure_summary",
#       data=portfolio_df,                 # must contain a signed `pos` column
#       pos="pos",
#       nav=1_000_000.0,
#   )
#   # -> portfolio_df + columns: gross, net, long, short, leverage
# =============================================================================

[[template]]
name = "exposure_summary"
description = "COMPOSITE projection (per-row, not aggregate): exposure breakdown (gross/net/long/short) over a signed position column plus a leverage ratio against a Number NAV."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "pos"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "nav"
kind = "number"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, gross_exposure({{pos}}) AS gross, net_exposure({{pos}}) AS net, long_exposure({{pos}}) AS long, short_exposure({{pos}}) AS short, leverage(gross_exposure({{pos}}), {{nav}}) AS leverage FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { pos = "pos", nav = 1000000.0 }

description: Per-group CAPM beta of `asset` returns vs `market` returns.
source:
# capm_beta
#
# Per-group CAPM beta of an asset's returns against the market's returns.
# Beta = cov(asset, market) / var(market), the slope of the asset's excess
# returns regressed on the market's. A grouped rollup: one beta per group.
#
# Run it:
#   quant-fabric local --templates ./templates --template capm_beta \
#     --arg data=returns.parquet \
#     --arg group_by=ticker \
#     --arg asset=stock_ret \
#     --arg market=mkt_ret

[[template]]
name = "capm_beta"
description = "Per-group CAPM beta of `asset` returns vs `market` returns."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "group_by"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "asset"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "market"
kind = "column"

[template.plan]
group_by = ["{{group_by}}"]
source_sql = "SELECT * FROM input"
abi_version = 2

[[template.plan.aggregate]]
output = "beta"
function = "beta"
inputs = ["{{asset}}", "{{market}}"]

source:
# factor_r2 — per-group goodness-of-fit (R²) of a linear factor model.
#
# Fits an OLS regression of `response` on one or more `regressors`
# (with an auto-added intercept) within each `group_by` partition, then
# reports the coefficient of determination (R²) describing how much of
# the response variance the factors explain.
#
# Run it:
#   quant-fabric local --templates ./templates --template factor_r2 \
#     --arg data=returns.parquet \
#     --arg group_by=sector \
#     --arg response=stock_return \
#     --arg regressors=mkt_excess,smb,hml

[[template]]
name = "factor_r2"
description = "Per-group R² of an OLS regression of `response` on `regressors`."
[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"
[[template.inputs]]
name = "group_by"
kind = "column"
[[template.inputs]]
name = "response"
kind = "column"
[[template.inputs]]
name = "regressors"
kind = "columns"
[template.plan]
group_by = ["{{group_by}}"]
source_sql = "SELECT * FROM input"
abi_version = 2
[template.plan.vectors]
design = ["{{response}}", "{{regressors}}"]
[[template.plan.aggregate]]
output = "r2"
function = "ols_fit"
inputs = "@design"
params = { statistic = 1, index = 0 }

name: factor_tstats
description: Per-group OLS t-statistic for each factor regressor.
source:
# factor_tstats
#
# Per-group OLS regression of `response` on a set of `regressors`, emitting the
# t-statistic for each factor's coefficient (one output column per regressor).
# The design vector splats `response` plus the `regressors` columns into the
# auto-intercept OLS; the for_each fans out one t-stat aggregate per factor,
# indexing the design at the factor's ordinal position (1-based, since 0 is the
# intercept).
#
# Run it:
#   quant-fabric local --templates ./templates --template factor_tstats \

#     --arg response=ret_fwd \

name: hedge_ratio
description: Per-group OLS slope of `y` on `x` — the pairs-trading hedge ratio.
source:
# hedge_ratio — per-group OLS hedge ratio for pairs trading.
#
# Fits an ordinary least squares regression of the dependent series `y` on the
# hedging instrument `x` (with an auto-intercept) within each group, and emits
# the slope coefficient on `x` as `hedge_ratio`. This slope is the classic
# pairs-trading hedge ratio: how many units of `x` to hold against one unit of
# `y` to neutralise the spread.
#
# The design vector is [y, x], so the response is index 0 and `x` is the first
# (and only) regressor at design index 1. statistic = 0 selects the coefficient.
#
# Run it:
#   quant-fabric local --templates ./templates --template hedge_ratio \
#     --arg data=prices.parquet \
#     --arg group_by=pair_id \
#     --arg y=spy_ret \
#     --arg x=ivv_ret

[[template]]
name = "hedge_ratio"
description = "Per-group OLS slope of `y` on `x` — the pairs-trading hedge ratio."
[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"
[[template.inputs]]
name = "group_by"
kind = "column"
[[template.inputs]]
name = "y"
kind = "column"
[[template.inputs]]
name = "x"
kind = "column"
[template.plan]
group_by = ["{{group_by}}"]
source_sql = "SELECT * FROM input"
abi_version = 2
[template.plan.vectors]
design = ["{{y}}", "{{x}}"]
[[template.plan.aggregate]]
output = "hedge_ratio"
function = "ols_fit"
inputs = "@design"
params = { statistic = 0, index = 1 }

# =============================================================================

# compounded rate over a time horizon:  FV = future_value(present_value, rate, ttm).
#
# UDF: future_value(present_value, rate, ttm)  -- ternary (quant_core::future_value)
#   - present_value : per-row amount to grow forward (bind to a price/spot column)
#   - rate          : annualized rate (scalar config -> Number input)
#   - ttm           : time to maturity in years (scalar config -> Number input)
#
# The per-row market input (the amount) is a Column; rate and ttm are scalar
# configuration supplied as Number inputs. Result is aliased to the `output`
# column (default: fv).
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *, future_value("spot", 0.05, 2.0) AS fv FROM input
#   -- grows each row's spot price forward 2 years at a 5% rate.
# =============================================================================

[[template]]
name = "future_value"
description = "Future value of a per-row amount grown forward at `rate` over `ttm` years, as a new `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "amount"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "rate"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "ttm"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, future_value({{amount}}, {{rate}}, {{ttm}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { amount = "spot", rate = 0.05, ttm = 2.0, output = "fv" }

name: present_value
description: Discount a future cash amount (column) to present value at a given rate over a time horizon, as a new `output` column.
source:
# ============================================================================
# Template: present_value  (category: Fixed Income)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Discounts a future cash amount back to its present value using continuous
# compounding:
#
#     present_value(future_value, rate, ttm) = future_value * exp(-rate * ttm)
#
# UDF arg order (READ from quant-core/src/lib.rs):
#     present_value(future_value: f64, rate: f64, ttm: f64)
#
# Bindings (per ADR-0020 conventions):
#   - future_value -> a per-row column (the cash amount), bound to `spot`
#   - rate         -> Number input (scalar config), e.g. 0.05 (5% per year)
#   - ttm          -> Number input (scalar config), e.g. 2.0 years
#   - output       -> Column input naming the result alias (pv)
#
# Run it:
#   present_value of each row's `spot` cash flow at a 5% rate over 2 years,
#   writing the discounted value into a new column `pv`:
#
#     SELECT *, present_value("spot", 0.05, 2.0) AS pv FROM input
#
#   A spot of 100 -> 100 * exp(-0.05 * 2.0) = 90.4837...
# ============================================================================

[[template]]
name = "present_value"
description = "Discount a future cash amount (column) to present value at a given rate over a time horizon, as a new `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "future_value"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "rate"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "ttm"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, present_value({{future_value}}, {{rate}}, {{ttm}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { future_value = "spot", rate = 0.05, ttm = 2.0, output = "pv" }

description: Present value of a zero-coupon bond: face_value * exp(-rate * ttm), emitted as a new `output` column.
source:
# =============================================================================
# Template: zero_coupon_price
# Category: Fixed Income
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prices a zero-coupon bond (ZCB) by discounting its face value to present
# value under continuous compounding:
#
#     zcb = face_value * exp(-rate * ttm)
#
# UDF signature (read from quant-core/src/lib.rs):
#     zero_coupon_price(face_value: f64, rate: f64, ttm: f64) -> Option<f64>
#
# Argument binding:
#   - face_value -> per-row Column (bond face/redemption value, here `spot`)
#   - rate       -> Number input (flat continuously-compounded discount rate)
#   - ttm        -> Number input (time to maturity, in years)
#
# Run it:
#   Bind `face` to your face-value column, set the discount `rate` and time to
#   maturity `ttm` as scalar config, and name the result column via `output`.
#   e.g. face = "spot", rate = 0.05, ttm = 2.0, output = "zcb"
#   -> SELECT *, zero_coupon_price("spot", 0.05, 2.0) AS zcb FROM input
# =============================================================================

[[template]]
name = "zero_coupon_price"
description = "Present value of a zero-coupon bond: face_value * exp(-rate * ttm), emitted as a new `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "face"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "rate"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "ttm"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, zero_coupon_price({{face}}, {{rate}}, {{ttm}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { face = "spot", rate = 0.05, ttm = 2.0, output = "zcb" }

name: effective_spread
description: Per-row signed effective spread: 2 * sign(side) * (trade_px - ref_px), emitted as a new `output` column.
source:
# =============================================================================
# Template: effective_spread
# Category: Microstructure
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Computes the per-row effective spread of an execution against a reference
# (mid) price, signed by the trade side.
#
#   effective_spread(execution_price, mid_price, signed_side)
#     = 2 * sign(signed_side) * (execution_price - mid_price)
#
# Argument order (from quant_core::effective_spread):
#   1. execution_price  -> trade_px   (per-row trade/execution price)
#   2. mid_price        -> ref_px     (per-row reference / mid price)
#   3. signed_side      -> side       (Number: +1 buy / -1 sell)
#
# The result is twice the signed deviation of the fill from the reference,
# so a marketable buy above mid (or sell below mid) yields a positive spread.
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *,
#          effective_spread("trade_px", "ref_px", 1.0) AS eff_spread
#   FROM input;
#   -- e.g. trade_px=101, ref_px=100, side=+1  ->  eff_spread = 2.0
# =============================================================================

[[template]]
name = "effective_spread"
description = "Per-row signed effective spread: 2 * sign(side) * (trade_px - ref_px), emitted as a new `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "trade_px"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "ref_px"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "side"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, effective_spread({{trade_px}}, {{ref_px}}, {{side}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { trade_px = "trade_px", ref_px = "ref_px", side = 1.0, output = "eff_spread" }

name: microprice
description: Size-weighted micro price from best bid/ask quotes and their sizes, emitted as a new `output` column.
source:
# microprice — size-weighted micro price from top-of-book quotes
#
# Computes the microprice, a size-weighted blend of the best bid and ask:
#   microprice = (bid * ask_size + ask * bid_size) / (bid_size + ask_size)
# It leans toward the side with LESS size (the side more likely to be hit),
# giving a fairer estimate of the underlying value than a plain mid price.
#
# UDF: microprice(bid, ask, bid_size, ask_size)  [quaternary scalar]
#   -> quant_core::microprice(bid, ask, bid_size, ask_size) -> Option<f64>
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *, microprice("bid", "ask", "bid_sz", "ask_sz") AS microprice
#   FROM input;

[[template]]
name = "microprice"
description = "Size-weighted micro price from best bid/ask quotes and their sizes, emitted as a new `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "bid"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "ask"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "bid_sz"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "ask_sz"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, microprice({{bid}}, {{ask}}, {{bid_sz}}, {{ask_sz}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { bid = "bid", ask = "ask", bid_sz = "bid_sz", ask_sz = "ask_sz", output = "microprice" }

name: mid_price
description: Per-row mid price (bid + ask) / 2 as a new `output` column.
source:
# =============================================================================
# Template: mid_price
# Category: Microstructure
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Computes the mid price of a quoted instrument as the simple average of the
# best bid and best ask: mid = (bid + ask) / 2.
#
# UDF: mid_price(bid, ask)  -- binary scalar (quant_core::mid_price)
#      bid: best bid price
#      ask: best ask price
#
# Run it:
#   Bind `bid` and `ask` to per-row quote columns and pick an output alias.
#   args = { bid = "bid", ask = "ask", output = "mid" }
#   -> SELECT *, mid_price("bid", "ask") AS "mid" FROM input
# =============================================================================

[[template]]
name = "mid_price"
description = "Per-row mid price (bid + ask) / 2 as a new `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "bid"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "ask"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, mid_price({{bid}}, {{ask}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { bid = "bid", ask = "ask", output = "mid" }

# Computes the order book imbalance from top-of-book sizes:
#     imbalance = (bid_size - ask_size) / (bid_size + ask_size)

#
# UDF: order_book_imbalance(bid_size, ask_size)  [binary scalar]
#   READ arg order: (bid_size, ask_size)
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *, order_book_imbalance("bid_sz", "ask_sz") AS imbalance FROM input
#
# Example over book snapshots:
#   bid_sz=500, ask_sz=300  ->  imbalance = 0.25  (buyers leaning in)
# =============================================================================

kind = "column"

name: quote_metrics
description: COMPOSITE projection (per-row, not aggregate): top-of-book metrics mid_price, microprice, quoted_spread, and order_book_imbalance in one SELECT over bid/ask prices and sizes.
source:
# quote_metrics — top-of-book microstructure summary (COMPOSITE)
#
# Emits four standard quote metrics in a single SELECT over the top-of-book
# inputs (best bid/ask price and their resting sizes):
#   * mid_price            = (bid + ask) / 2
#   * microprice           = size-weighted fair value: leans toward the side
#                            with MORE depth (ask_size weights the bid, etc.)
#   * quoted_spread        = ask - bid (absolute width of the quote)
#   * order_book_imbalance = (bid_size - ask_size) / (bid_size + ask_size),
#                            in [-1, 1]; >0 means bid-heavy book
#
# This is a COMPOSITE template: there is no single `output` input; each metric
# is written to its own fixed output column.
#
# UDFs: mid_price(bid, ask), microprice(bid, ask, bid_size, ask_size),
#       quoted_spread(bid, ask), order_book_imbalance(bid_size, ask_size)
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *,
#          mid_price(bid, ask)                        AS mid_price,
#          microprice(bid, ask, bid_sz, ask_sz)       AS microprice,
#          quoted_spread(bid, ask)                    AS quoted_spread,
#          order_book_imbalance(bid_sz, ask_sz)       AS order_book_imbalance
#   FROM quotes;

[[template]]
name = "quote_metrics"
description = "COMPOSITE projection (per-row, not aggregate): top-of-book metrics mid_price, microprice, quoted_spread, and order_book_imbalance in one SELECT over bid/ask prices and sizes."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "bid"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "ask"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "bid_size"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "ask_size"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, mid_price({{bid}}, {{ask}}) AS mid_price, microprice({{bid}}, {{ask}}, {{bid_size}}, {{ask_size}}) AS microprice, quoted_spread({{bid}}, {{ask}}) AS quoted_spread, order_book_imbalance({{bid_size}}, {{ask_size}}) AS order_book_imbalance FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { bid = "bid", ask = "ask", bid_size = "bid_sz", ask_size = "ask_sz" }

name: quoted_spread
description: Per-row quoted spread (ask - bid) of a two-sided market as a new `output` column.
source:
# =============================================================================
# Template: quoted_spread
# Category: Microstructure
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Computes the quoted spread of a two-sided market: the absolute gap between
# the best ask and best bid (ask - bid). It is the most basic measure of
# transaction-cost / liquidity at the top of book.
#
#   quoted_spread(bid, ask) = ask - bid
#
# (A relative variant, quoted_spread_bps(bid, ask), expresses the same gap in
#  basis points of the mid price -- see the quoted_spread_bps template.)
#
# UDF: quoted_spread(bid, ask)  -- binary scalar
#   quant_core::quoted_spread(bid: f64, ask: f64) -> Option<f64>
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *, quoted_spread(bid, ask) AS spread
#   FROM   quotes;
#   -- bid=99.0, ask=101.0  ->  spread = 2.0
# =============================================================================

[[template]]
name = "quoted_spread"
description = "Per-row quoted spread (ask - bid) of a two-sided market as a new `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "bid"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "ask"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, quoted_spread({{bid}}, {{ask}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { bid = "bid", ask = "ask", output = "spread" }

name: deflated_sharpe
description: Deflated Sharpe Ratio: PSR against the expected-max Sharpe benchmark, correcting for multiple-testing bias. Emits an `output` column.
source:
# =============================================================================
# Template: deflated_sharpe
# Category: Performance
# =============================================================================
# Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) — Bailey & Lopez de Prado.
#
# The DSR is the Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio evaluated against an
# expected-maximum Sharpe benchmark, correcting for multiple-testing /
# selection bias when a strategy is the best of many trials. It returns the
# probability (0..1) that the true Sharpe exceeds that benchmark, adjusting
# for sample length, return skewness, and excess kurtosis.
#
# UDF: deflated_sharpe_ratio(observed_sr, n_obs, skewness, excess_kurtosis,
#                            n_trials, variance_of_trial_srs)
#   - observed_sr            : the candidate strategy's observed Sharpe ratio
#   - n_obs                  : number of return observations (BIGINT)
#   - skewness               : skewness of the strategy returns
#   - excess_kurtosis        : excess kurtosis (kurtosis - 3) of the returns
#   - n_trials               : number of strategy configurations tried (BIGINT)
#   - variance_of_trial_srs  : variance of the Sharpe ratios across trials
#
# All six arguments are scalar configuration values (not per-row market data),
# so each is bound to a NUMBER input with a realistic literal.
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *, deflated_sharpe_ratio(1.25, 250, -0.3, 2.5, 100, 0.5) AS dsr
#   FROM input;
# =============================================================================

[[template]]
name = "deflated_sharpe"
description = "Deflated Sharpe Ratio: PSR against the expected-max Sharpe benchmark, correcting for multiple-testing bias. Emits an `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "observed_sr"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "n_obs"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "skewness"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "excess_kurtosis"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "n_trials"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "variance_of_trial_srs"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, deflated_sharpe_ratio({{observed_sr}}, {{n_obs}}, {{skewness}}, {{excess_kurtosis}}, {{n_trials}}, {{variance_of_trial_srs}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { observed_sr = 1.25, n_obs = 250, skewness = -0.3, excess_kurtosis = 2.5, n_trials = 100, variance_of_trial_srs = 0.5, output = "dsr" }

name: information_ratio
description: Per-row Information Ratio (active_return / tracking_error) as a new `output` column.
source:
# ============================================================================
# Performance / information_ratio
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per-row Information Ratio = active_return / tracking_error.
#
# Measures risk-adjusted active performance: how much excess return (active
# return relative to a benchmark) is earned per unit of tracking error
# (the volatility of that active return). Higher is better; it is undefined
# when tracking error is non-positive.
#
# UDF: information_ratio(active_return, tracking_error)  [binary scalar]
#   arg 1 = active_return   -> column `a`
#   arg 2 = tracking_error  -> a strictly-positive column (e.g. `vol`); the
#                              ratio is undefined when tracking error <= 0
#   output alias            -> ir
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *, information_ratio(active_ret, tracking_err) AS ir FROM input
# ============================================================================

[[template]]
name = "information_ratio"
description = "Per-row Information Ratio (active_return / tracking_error) as a new `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "active_return"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "tracking_error"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, information_ratio({{active_return}}, {{tracking_error}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { active_return = "a", tracking_error = "vol", output = "ir" }

name: probabilistic_sharpe
description: Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio: probability the true Sharpe beats a benchmark, adjusted for sample size, skewness, and excess kurtosis. Result aliased as `output`.
source:
# probabilistic_sharpe — Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio (Bailey & López de Prado 2012)
#
# Computes PSR: the probability that a strategy's *true* Sharpe ratio exceeds a
# benchmark Sharpe (often 0), correcting the observed Sharpe for sample length
# and the return distribution's skewness and excess kurtosis.
#
#   PSR = Φ( (SR − SR*)·√(n−1) / √(1 − γ₃·SR + ((γ₄−1)/4)·SR²) )
#
# UDF: probabilistic_sharpe_ratio(observed_sr, benchmark_sr, n, skewness, excess_kurtosis)
#   observed_sr     DOUBLE  — the strategy's measured Sharpe ratio
#   benchmark_sr    DOUBLE  — the Sharpe threshold to beat (SR*), e.g. 0.0
#   n               BIGINT  — number of return observations (n >= 2)
#   skewness        DOUBLE  — γ₃ of the returns
#   excess_kurtosis DOUBLE  — γ₄ − 3 of the returns (0 for normal)
# All five are scalar configuration values -> NUMBER inputs (n is integer-valued).
#
# Run it:
#   probabilistic_sharpe(observed_sr=1.25, benchmark_sr=0.0, n=252, skewness=-0.5,
#                        excess_kurtosis=3.0, output="psr")
#   -> appends a `psr` column (probability in [0,1]) to every row of `data`.

[[template]]
name = "probabilistic_sharpe"
description = "Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio: probability the true Sharpe beats a benchmark, adjusted for sample size, skewness, and excess kurtosis. Result aliased as `output`."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "observed_sr"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "benchmark_sr"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "n"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "skewness"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "excess_kurtosis"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, probabilistic_sharpe_ratio({{observed_sr}}, {{benchmark_sr}}, CAST({{n}} AS BIGINT), {{skewness}}, {{excess_kurtosis}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { observed_sr = 1.25, benchmark_sr = 0.0, n = 252, skewness = -0.5, excess_kurtosis = 3.0, output = "psr" }

name: max_diversification_weights
description: Maximum-diversification portfolio weight per asset over the supplied return universe.
source:
# max_diversification_weights
#
# Global covariance-matrix fan-out that emits one maximum-diversification
# portfolio weight per asset. Builds the covariance matrix over the supplied
# asset-return columns, then for each asset returns its weight in the
# maximum-diversification portfolio (covariance_matrix stat = 6, indexed by
# the asset's position in the universe).
#
# Run it:
#   quant-fabric local --templates ./templates --template max_diversification_weights \
#     --table data \
#     --assets ret_spy,ret_tlt,ret_gld,ret_vnq
#
# Emits md_weight_ret_spy, md_weight_ret_tlt, md_weight_ret_gld,
# md_weight_ret_vnq as a single global reduce row.

[[template]]
name = "max_diversification_weights"
description = "Maximum-diversification portfolio weight per asset over the supplied return universe."
[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"
[[template.inputs]]
name = "assets"
kind = "columns"
[template.plan]
group_by = []
source_sql = "SELECT * FROM input"
abi_version = 2
[template.plan.vectors]
universe = ["{{assets}}"]
[[template.plan.aggregate]]
for_each = "assets"
output = "md_weight_{{item}}"
function = "covariance_matrix"
inputs = "@universe"
params = { stat = 6, i = "{{index}}" }

name: min_variance_weights
description: Global minimum-variance portfolio weights (Σ⁻¹𝟙 / 𝟙ᵀΣ⁻¹𝟙) over `assets`, from the distributed covariance matrix.
source:
# Global minimum-variance portfolio weights over a set of asset return columns,
# computed from the distributed covariance matrix (Chan parallel merge on the
# coordinator) — one weight per asset via a `for_each` fan-out.
#
#   quant-fabric local --templates ./templates --template min_variance_weights \
#     --arg data=returns.parquet --arg assets=spy,tlt,gld
#
# Emits one row of weight_<asset> columns (global reduce — no group_by).

[[template]]
name = "min_variance_weights"
description = "Global minimum-variance portfolio weights (Σ⁻¹𝟙 / 𝟙ᵀΣ⁻¹𝟙) over `assets`, from the distributed covariance matrix."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"
[[template.inputs]]
name = "assets"
kind = "columns"       # >= 2 asset return columns

[template.plan]
group_by = []          # global reduce — one portfolio over the whole sample
source_sql = "SELECT * FROM input"
abi_version = 2

[template.plan.vectors]
universe = ["{{assets}}"]

# One min-variance weight per asset. `{{index}}` (0-based) selects the asset row
# of the covariance matrix; stat = 2 is the min-variance weight finalizer.
[[template.plan.aggregate]]
for_each = "assets"
output = "weight_{{item}}"
function = "covariance_matrix"
inputs = "@universe"
params = { stat = 2, i = "{{index}}" }

name: adf_critical_value
description: ADF unit-root test critical value for a given regression specification and significance level, emitted as the `adf_cv` column.
source:
# ============================================================================
# adf_critical_value — Augmented Dickey-Fuller critical value lookup
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Returns the MacKinnon critical value for the ADF unit-root test, used to
# decide whether a time series (or residual spread) is stationary. Compare a
# computed ADF test statistic against this critical value: if the statistic is
# more negative than the critical value, reject the unit-root null (the series
# is stationary / mean-reverting — e.g. a tradable pairs spread).
#
# UDF: adf_critical_value(regression_type, significance)
#   regression_type — model specification code:
#       0 = no constant
#       1 = constant (drift)
#       2 = constant + trend
#   significance    — test level: 0.01, 0.05, or 0.10
# Both arguments are scalar configuration, bound to Number inputs.
# Returns NULL for unsupported codes/levels.
#
# Run it:
#   adf_critical_value(regression_type = 1, significance = 0.05) -> -2.8621
#   (constant model, 5% level). Every row gets the same critical value column,
#   ready to compare against a per-row ADF statistic.
# ============================================================================

[[template]]
name = "adf_critical_value"
description = "ADF unit-root test critical value for a given regression specification and significance level, emitted as the `adf_cv` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "regression_type"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "significance"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, adf_critical_value({{regression_type}}, {{significance}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { regression_type = 1, significance = 0.05, output = "adf_cv" }

name: cornish_fisher_var
description: Cornish-Fisher adjusted quantile from a per-row z driver plus scalar skewness and excess kurtosis, output as `cf_quantile`.
source:
# cornish_fisher_var
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cornish-Fisher quantile expansion: adjusts a Gaussian quantile (z) for the
# skewness and excess kurtosis of the underlying distribution. Used to build a
# non-normal Value-at-Risk / quantile estimate that accounts for fat tails and
# asymmetry instead of assuming a textbook normal distribution.
#
# UDF: cornish_fisher_quantile(z, skewness, excess_kurtosis) -> ternary scalar
#   - z               : the (per-row) Gaussian quantile / probability driver -> column `prob`
#   - skewness        : distribution skew (scalar config) -> Number input
#   - excess_kurtosis : distribution excess kurtosis (scalar config) -> Number input
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *, cornish_fisher_quantile("prob", -0.5, 3.0) AS cf_quantile FROM input
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

[[template]]
name = "cornish_fisher_var"
description = "Cornish-Fisher adjusted quantile from a per-row z driver plus scalar skewness and excess kurtosis, output as `cf_quantile`."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "probability"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "skewness"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "kurtosis"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, cornish_fisher_quantile({{probability}}, {{skewness}}, {{kurtosis}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { probability = "prob", skewness = -0.5, kurtosis = 3.0, output = "cf_quantile" }

name: ou_half_life
description: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck mean-reversion half-life derived from an AR(1) coefficient, as a new `output` column.
source:
# ou_half_life — Ornstein-Uhlenbeck mean-reversion half-life
#
# Converts an AR(1) autoregression coefficient (phi) into the half-life of
# mean reversion: half_life = -ln(2) / ln(phi). This is the number of periods
# for a deviation from the long-run mean to decay by half. Defined only for
# 0 < phi < 1 (returns NULL otherwise, e.g. phi <= 0 or phi >= 1).
#
# UDF: ou_half_life(ar_coefficient) — unary
#   ar_coefficient : AR(1) coefficient phi (per-row), e.g. ~0.9
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *, ou_half_life(ar1) AS half_life FROM input
#   -- ou_half_life(0.9) ≈ 6.5788 periods
#
# Conventions: ADR-0020 scalar template; exactly one table input ("data");
# {{ar1_coefficient}} auto-quotes the column identifier; {{output}} is the alias.

[[template]]
name = "ou_half_life"
description = "Ornstein-Uhlenbeck mean-reversion half-life derived from an AR(1) coefficient, as a new `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "ar1_coefficient"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, ou_half_life({{ar1_coefficient}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { ar1_coefficient = "ar1", output = "half_life" }

name: pca_eigenvalues
description: Descending eigenvalues of the asset covariance matrix (PCA variance explained), one column per principal component.
source:
# pca_eigenvalues
#
# Descending eigenvalues of the covariance matrix across an asset universe.
# Each eigenvalue is the variance explained by the corresponding principal
# component (PCA), ordered largest-to-smallest. One output column per asset:
# `eigenvalue_1` is the leading (largest) eigenvalue, `eigenvalue_2` the next,
# and so on, via a covariance_matrix fan-out over the asset columns.
#
# Global reduce (group_by = []): collapses the whole table to a single row of
# eigenvalues for the supplied asset universe (>= 2 columns).
#
# Run it:
#   quant-fabric local --templates ./templates --template pca_eigenvalues \
#     --arg data=returns.parquet \
#     --arg assets='AAPL,MSFT,GOOG,AMZN'

[[template]]
name = "pca_eigenvalues"
description = "Descending eigenvalues of the asset covariance matrix (PCA variance explained), one column per principal component."
[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"
[[template.inputs]]
name = "assets"
kind = "columns"
[template.plan]
group_by = []
source_sql = "SELECT * FROM input"
abi_version = 2
[template.plan.vectors]
universe = ["{{assets}}"]
[[template.plan.aggregate]]
for_each = "assets"
output = "eigenvalue_{{ordinal}}"
function = "covariance_matrix"
inputs = "@universe"
params = { stat = 4, i = "{{index}}" }

name: fractional_kelly
description: Scale a per-row full Kelly fraction by a constant multiplier in [0, 1] (e.g. half-Kelly), emitted as the `output` column.
source:
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# fractional_kelly — scale a full Kelly fraction by a constant in [0, 1].
#
# UDF: fractional_kelly(kelly_fraction, fraction)
#   arg1 kelly_fraction : the full Kelly betting fraction f* (per-row column)
#   arg2 fraction       : scaling multiplier in [0, 1] (e.g. 0.5 for half-Kelly)
# Returns f* * fraction; NULL when `fraction` is outside [0, 1].
#
# Full Kelly is notoriously aggressive and sensitive to estimation error, so
# practitioners commonly apply a fractional (e.g. half-Kelly) overlay to damp
# drawdowns. This scalar template appends the scaled bet size as `frac_kelly`.
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *, fractional_kelly("prob", 0.5) AS frac_kelly FROM input
#   (here `prob` carries the per-row full Kelly fraction; 0.5 -> half-Kelly)
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[[template]]
name = "fractional_kelly"
description = "Scale a per-row full Kelly fraction by a constant multiplier in [0, 1] (e.g. half-Kelly), emitted as the `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "kelly_fraction"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "fraction"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, fractional_kelly({{kelly_fraction}}, {{fraction}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { kelly_fraction = "prob", fraction = 0.5, output = "frac_kelly" }

name: kelly_fraction
description: Growth-optimal Kelly fraction f* = expected_excess_return / variance as a new `output` column.
source:
# kelly_fraction — optimal Kelly bet sizing
#
# Computes the full Kelly fraction f* = expected_excess_return / variance,
# the growth-optimal allocation for a single risky bet/asset given its edge
# (expected return in excess of the risk-free rate) and its variance.
#
# UDF: kelly_fraction(expected_excess_return, variance)  [binary scalar]
#   - expected_excess_return : per-row edge (bound to column `a`)
#   - variance               : variance of returns (scalar Number input)
# Returns NULL when variance <= 0.
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *, kelly_fraction("a", 0.04) AS kelly FROM input;
#   -- e.g. edge a=0.08, variance=0.04  ->  kelly = 2.0

[[template]]
name = "kelly_fraction"
description = "Growth-optimal Kelly fraction f* = expected_excess_return / variance as a new `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "expected_excess_return"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "variance"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, kelly_fraction({{expected_excess_return}}, {{variance}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { expected_excess_return = "a", variance = 0.04, output = "kelly" }

name: position_sizing
description: COMPOSITE projection (per-row, not aggregate): Kelly fraction, fractional (safety-scaled) Kelly, and vol-target leverage scale in one SELECT.
source:
# ============================================================================
# Template: position_sizing  (COMPOSITE)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Emits three position-sizing columns in a single SELECT:
#   - kelly_fraction   : optimal Kelly bet = expected_excess_return / variance
#   - fractional_kelly : Kelly fraction scaled by a (0..1) safety fraction
#   - vol_target_scale : leverage to hit a target vol = target_vol / realized_vol
#
# UDFs (binary scalars, arg order from quant-core source):
#   kelly_fraction(expected_excess_return, variance)
#   fractional_kelly(kelly_fraction, fraction)
#   vol_target_scale(target_vol, realized_vol)
#
# Per-row market inputs are bound to dataset columns; scalar config
# (kelly_fraction safety fraction, target vol) are NUMBER inputs.
#
# Run it:
#   quant-fabric run --template position_sizing \
#     --arg excess_return=a --arg variance=vol --arg realized_vol=vol \
#     --arg kelly_fraction=0.5 --arg target_vol=0.1 \
#     --data positions.csv
# ============================================================================

[[template]]
name = "position_sizing"
description = "COMPOSITE projection (per-row, not aggregate): Kelly fraction, fractional (safety-scaled) Kelly, and vol-target leverage scale in one SELECT."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "excess_return"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "variance"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "realized_vol"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "kelly_fraction"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "target_vol"
kind = "number"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, kelly_fraction({{excess_return}}, {{variance}}) AS kelly_fraction, fractional_kelly(kelly_fraction({{excess_return}}, {{variance}}), {{kelly_fraction}}) AS fractional_kelly, vol_target_scale({{target_vol}}, {{realized_vol}}) AS vol_target_scale FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { excess_return = "a", variance = "vol", realized_vol = "vol", kelly_fraction = 0.5, target_vol = 0.1 }

name: vol_target_scale
description: Per-row volatility-targeting scale factor target_vol / realized_vol as a new `output` column.
source:
# =============================================================================
# Sizing / vol_target_scale
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Volatility-targeting position scale factor.
#
#   vol_scale = target_vol / realized_vol
#
# Multiply a base position by this factor to size it so that the resulting
# exposure carries the desired (target) annualised volatility, given the
# asset's realized volatility. A realized vol of 0 yields NULL (undefined).
#
# UDF: vol_target_scale(target_vol, realized_vol)  -- binary scalar
#   arg 0: target_vol   -> Number input  (scalar config, e.g. 0.10 = 10% target)
#   arg 1: realized_vol -> Column input  (per-row realized vol, bound to `vol`)
#
# Run it:
#   target_vol = 0.10, realized_vol = vol (~0.20)
#   -> vol_scale = 0.10 / 0.20 = 0.50
# =============================================================================

[[template]]
name = "vol_target_scale"
description = "Per-row volatility-targeting scale factor target_vol / realized_vol as a new `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "target_vol"
kind = "number"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "realized_vol"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, vol_target_scale({{target_vol}}, {{realized_vol}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { target_vol = 0.10, realized_vol = "vol", output = "vol_scale" }

# log_returns — per-row logarithmic return

# Computes the continuously-compounded (log) return between a starting price and
# an ending price: log_return(start_price, end_price) = ln(end_price / start_price).
# Log returns are time-additive, which makes them convenient for aggregating
# returns across consecutive periods.

#   -- price0 = prior price, price1 = current price; ret_log = ln(price1/price0)

kind = "table"

name: normal_inverse_cdf
description: Per-row standard normal quantile (probit): z such that Phi(z) = prob, as a new `output` column.
source:
# normal_inverse_cdf — standard normal quantile (probit) function
#
# Maps a cumulative probability p in (0, 1) to the z-score where the
# standard normal CDF equals p, i.e. z such that Phi(z) = p. This is the
# inverse of the standard normal CDF and is the building block for
# VaR/quantile conversions, confidence-interval bounds, and Gaussian
# scenario generation.
#
# Unary scalar: normal_inverse_cdf(prob) -> z
#   prob : per-row cumulative probability in (0, 1)
#
# Run it:
#   SELECT *, normal_inverse_cdf(prob) AS z FROM input;
#   -- prob = 0.5 -> z ~ 0.0 ; prob = 0.975 -> z ~ 1.96

[[template]]
name = "normal_inverse_cdf"
description = "Per-row standard normal quantile (probit): z such that Phi(z) = prob, as a new `output` column."

[[template.inputs]]
name = "data"
kind = "table"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "prob"
kind = "column"

[[template.inputs]]
name = "output"
kind = "column"

[template.sql]
template = "SELECT *, normal_inverse_cdf({{prob}}) AS {{output}} FROM input"

[template.example]
args = { prob = "prob", output = "z" }
